result.markdown: --- title: "[Graph.is_edge_cover()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method}" body-classes: doc-api-page doc-py-api-page shift-heading-level-by: 0 toc-depth: 3 page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Check if a set of edges touches every node (an edge cover). ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/edgecase/blob/main/python/edgecase/graph.py#L58362-L58411){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python Graph.is_edge_cover(edges) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} ![Is edge cover](/assets/graphs/is-edge-cover.light.svg){.lightbox fig-alt="The path A-B-C-D on both sides, with the candidate edges drawn as the input. Left: the outer edges A-B and C-D touch all four nodes, so is_edge_cover() returns True. Right: the middle edge B-C alone misses A and D (filled in the accent color), so is_edge_cover() returns False." width="100%"} An edge cover is a set of edges such that every node of the graph is an endpoint of at least one of them. Unlike a matching, edges in a cover may share endpoints. Use this method to validate a hand-built cover or the output of `min_edge_cover()`. A graph with an isolated node has no edge cover, so the check is then always `False` (and the empty graph is covered by the empty set). ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [edges]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [list[int]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : A list of integer edge IDs. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [bool]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : `True` if every node is an endpoint of one of the edges. Unknown edge IDs give `False`. ::: ## Technical Notes {.doc-technical-notes} The check collects the endpoints of the given edges and compares them with the node set, in $O(V + k)$ time for $k$ edges. Edge direction is ignored. ## Examples {.doc-examples} The two outer edges of the path A-B-C-D cover all four nodes, while the middle edge alone misses A and D: ::: {#80d5e232 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec g = ec.Graph().add_nodes(["A", "B", "C", "D"]) g.add_edges([("A", "B"), ("B", "C"), ("C", "D")]) ab, bc, cd = (g.find_edge_ids(u, v)[0] for u, v in [("A", "B"), ("B", "C"), ("C", "D")]) g.is_edge_cover([ab, cd]), g.is_edge_cover([bc]) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` (True, False) ``` ::: :::
